name: Hubstaff
tagline: Track opt-in work time without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring
verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Hubstaff, track opt-in work time without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring. The hard boundary is workforce tracking, payroll, gps, scheduling, reports, and compliance operations, plus ubiquitous capture, coaching, and team workflow.
coreLoopDIY: Track opt-in work time and focused sessions without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring, review patterns locally, and export a transparent activity record.
requirements: optional accessibility permission for app-name tracking
whatYouLose: workforce tracking, payroll, GPS, scheduling, reports, and compliance operations
moatNotes: ubiquitous capture, coaching, and team workflow
ongoingBurden: idle detection, permissions, app metadata, privacy, notifications, sync, reports, integrations, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Hubstaff because the timer is simple, but people pay for frictionless capture and a history they trust enough to invoice or change habits from. The recurring cost buys idle detection, permissions, app metadata, privacy, notifications, sync, reports, integrations, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Kimai
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source time-tracking application with projects, reports, and exports.

alternatives.name: Clockify Free
alternatives.desc: Five users get timers and a private auto-tracker; reports stop at 31-day windows and CSV export is paid.

alternatives.name: Kimai
alternatives.desc: Timesheets, rates, reports and invoices are all there; approvals need its free plugin and the server still needs an adult.

alternatives.name: solidtime
alternatives.desc: Modern multi-user timers, clients and billable rates in one Compose stack; the desktop apps are still beta.

alternatives.name: Super Productivity
alternatives.desc: Projects, timesheets, reports and break reminders live in one local app; no manager surveillance dashboard attached.

alternatives.name: TimeCamp Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited people and projects get timers, auto-tracking and a personal activity timeline; app analytics and approvals are paid.

alternatives.name: TimeTagger
alternatives.desc: A lean timeline, tags and PDF or CSV reports in one container; it is built for individuals, not payroll departments.

alternatives.name: Toggl Track Free
alternatives.desc: Five users get fast timers, projects, tags and reports; approvals and paid-time controls cost extra.

alternatives.name: Traggo
alternatives.desc: A tiny tag-based timer with useful dashboards in one container; invoices and mobile apps never arrive.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal desktop tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Hubstaff in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and optional OS accessibility APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track opt-in work time and focused sessions without screenshots, keystrokes, or hidden monitoring, review patterns locally, and export a transparent activity record.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create one-click start and stop, manual entries, idle detection, tags, projects, and notes.
Keep any application-name tracking opt-in and never record window contents or keystrokes.
Add Pomodoro-style focus sessions, break reminders, and an optional allowlist blocker.
Provide daily, weekly, project, and category reports with editable corrections.
Export CSV and JSON and make the underlying event log inspectable.
Add automatic local backups and a privacy screen explaining every collected field.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out employee surveillance.
Deliberately leave out payroll and billing automation.
Deliberately leave out cross-device blocking and behavioral coaching services.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
